note: What the platform template drops. Read scripts/build-template.mjs and src/template-boundary.test.ts alongside this file — the test proves every entry here is real, and the script is the only thing that consumes it. Adding a product vertical means adding it here in the same commit; the boundary test fails otherwise.

regeneratedSnapshots.reason: The sidebar characterisation snapshots record the whole navigation tree, which the template legitimately changes by dropping four sections. Copying the product's snapshot would make the template fail on a difference that is the entire point of it. The build drops the file and the first test run records the template's own.

keptDeliberately.convex/settingsService.ts: The white-label navigation profiles list vertical nav keys in their `hide` arrays. Hiding a nav item that does not exist is a no-op, and keeping the catalogue intact means a product that later adds its own `properties` module inherits the same profile decisions. Removing them would mean editing a platform file to erase a vertical's name, which is exactly what the fence markers exist to avoid.
